summary: 1911 state fire lookout on Camel's Hump: a telephone line and a cement map table, never a tower; the table is listed as gone and no source describes remains.

facts.design: Cement map table with a telephone line; no tower was built
facts.status_note: Firelookout.org lists a Map Table as gone. No source describes any remains on the summit.

staffing.status: lookout posted through the 1911 fire season; watch in very dry weather; named lookoutman in 1916

access.note: The summit lies in Camel's Hump State Park and is reached on foot by trails.

visit.trail_note: Monroe Trail is somewhat challenging; an accessible loop has its own parking area and viewing spots toward the summit.

events.note: Telephone line built to the summit and a cement table constructed to hold the map; no tower was built
Lookout posted on the summit through the 1911 fire season
June 1912 report: an arrangement was made with the Waterbury Club, which kept a camp on the summit, to look for fires; a permanent shelter and trained watchman were planned
Station used only during very dry weather, at state expense
State report for 1916 credits lookoutman Mr. Chamberlin with cautioning over 500 people about leaving campfires burning

evidence.quote: Camel's Hump is soon to have the first fire lookout station ever to be established by the forest department.

evidence.supports: telephone line built to the summit in 1911 as the first lookout site
evidence.quote: In 1911 a telephone line was built to the summit of Camel's Hump to serve as the first lookout site.

evidence.supports: no tower was ever built; a cement table held the map
evidence.quote: No tower was ever built. Merely a cement table was constructed upon which the map of the country side was placed.

evidence.supports: June 1912 report: arrangement with Waterbury Club, which maintains a camp on the summit, to look for fires
evidence.quote: an arrangement was made with the Waterbury Club, which maintains a camp on the summit, to look for fires.

evidence.supports: 1913: station used only during very dry weather, at state expense
evidence.quote: is used only during very dry weather, and then at State expense.

evidence.quote: Mr. Chamberlin, the lookoutman on Camel's Hump, during the past year cautioned over 500 people in the woods in regard to leaving camp fires burning

corrections.proposed: map table (cement table with telephone line; no tower built)
corrections.why: Forest Lookouts quotes a Vermont forestry history saying no tower was ever built, and firelookout.org lists the site as a Map Table.

sources.title: Watching from above: The story of Vermont's fire towers

notes_for_editor: The 1911 start is backed by three sources. A Vermont State Parks blog photo caption calling this the first forest fire lookout in Vermont appeared only in a search result; that blog URL returned 404 when fetched, so it is not cited. The Daily Chronicle places the lookout 'around the same time' as the 1912-13 Burke Mountain tower but dates the watch to the 1911 fire season; the story uses 1911. The cement table's fate and any remains on the summit are not described by any source found, and the Forest Lookouts 'Removed' has no date.
